目前 dotfiles 裡**沒有** `git add -A && git commit -m` 的 alias 或 shell function。

現有 git 相關的只有：
- `alias lg='lazygit'` — 在 `dot_config/zsh/tools/37_lazygit.zsh`

---

想要新增的話，常見做法有兩種：

**1. 簡單 alias (gcam)**
```zsh
alias gcam='git add -A && git commit -m'
# 用法: gcam "your message"
```

**2. Shell function (更安全，可加防護)**
```zsh
gcam() {
  [[ -z "$1" ]] && { echo "Usage: gcam <message>"; return 1; }
  git add -A && git commit -m "$1"
}
```

要加到 `dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh` 嗎？還是你有其他偏好的風格或位置？

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-04-16 02:10:35Z)**_

加好了，新增了：

| 指令 | 功能 |
|------|------|
| `gcam "message"` | `git add -A && git commit -m "message"` |
| `gca` | `git commit --amend --no-edit`（保留原訊息） |
| `gcam-amend "new msg"` | `git commit --amend -m "new msg"`（改訊息） |
| `gundo` | `git reset --soft HEAD~1`，並印出被 undo 的 commit 訊息 |

19	
20	1. Add corresponding `ARG CHEZMOI_*` build argument

# Custom Aliases & Shell Functions

Quick reference for custom aliases and shell functions defined in this dotfiles repo.

> **Maintenance rule** (mirrored in `CLAUDE.md`): whenever you add or modify a custom alias or shell function, update this table — include the type, source file (relative to repo root), and a brief description.

## Reference Table

| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
| `v` | alias | `dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh` | Open Neovim (`nvim`) |
| `zsh-profile` | alias | `dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh` | Profile zsh startup time |
| `load-nvm` | alias | `dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh` | Lazy-load NVM for the current session |
| `bw-update-completion` | alias | `dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh` | Regenerate cached Bitwarden zsh completion |
| `ghostty-ssh-terminfo` | function | `dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh` | Install xterm-ghostty terminfo on a remote host over SSH |
| `gcam` | function | `dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh` | `git add -A && git commit -m "<msg>"` |
| `gca` | alias | `dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh` | `git commit --amend --no-edit` (keep existing message) |
| `gcam-amend` | function | `dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh` | `git commit --amend -m "<msg>"` (replace message) |
| `gundo` | function | `dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh` | Undo last commit → back to staged; prints undone commit message |
| `lg` | alias | `dot_config/zsh/tools/37_lazygit.zsh` | Open lazygit TUI |
| `ghget` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/41_github.zsh` | Download a subdirectory from a GitHub tree URL |

1	# 42_gitlab.zsh - GitLab helpers using glab CLI
2	
3	# ==============================================================================
4	# Method 1: Direct shell function (no AI agent needed)
5	# ==============================================================================
6	
7	# Create a GitLab repo under a group from the current git repo, set origin, and push.
8	# Detects current folder name as repo name and current branch automatically.
9	#
10	# Usage:
11	#   glcreate <group> [description]
12	#
13	# Examples:
14	#   glcreate david_quick_tries
15	#   glcreate david_quick_tries "My awesome project"
16	#
17	# If no description is given, the repo is created without one.
18	# The repo is created as private by default.
19	glcreate() {
20	  emulate -L zsh
21	
22	  local group="${1:?Usage: glcreate <group> [description]}"
23	  local desc="${2:-}"
24	  local name=$(basename "$(pwd)")
25	  local branch=$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "main")
26	
27	  echo "Creating: ${group}/${name} (branch: ${branch})"
28	
29	  glab repo create "${group}/${name}" \
30	    --private \
31	    --defaultBranch "$branch" \
32	    --skipGitInit \
33	    ${desc:+--description "$desc"} \
34	  && {
35	    # Add or update origin remote
36	    git remote add origin "git@gitlab.com:${group}/${name}.git" 2>/dev/null \
37	      || git remote set-url origin "git@gitlab.com:${group}/${name}.git"
38	  } \
39	  && git push -u origin "$branch"
40	}
41	
42	# ==============================================================================
43	# Method 2: AI agent assisted (summarizes description from project content)
44	# ==============================================================================
45	
46	# Create a GitLab repo using an AI coding agent to inspect the project,
47	# auto-generate a description, create the repo, set origin, and push.
48	#
49	# Supported agents: opencode (default), claude, codex, cursor-agent
50	# Set GLCREATE_AGENT to change the default agent.
51	# Set GLCREATE_LANG to change the default prompt language (zh or en, default: zh).
52	#
53	# Usage:
54	#   glcreate-ai <group> [description] [--agent <name>] [--lang zh|en]
55	#
56	# Examples:
57	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries
58	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries "Override description"
59	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries --agent claude
60	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries --lang en
61	#
62	# If no description is given, the agent will summarize one from the project content.
63	glcreate-ai() {
64	  emulate -L zsh
65	
66	  local group="" desc="" agent="${GLCREATE_AGENT:-opencode}" lang="${GLCREATE_LANG:-zh}"
67	
68	  # Parse arguments
69	  while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
70	    case "$1" in
71	      --agent) agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
72	      --lang)  lang="$2"; shift 2 ;;
73	      *) [[ -z "$group" ]] && group="$1" || desc="$1"; shift ;;
74	    esac
75	  done
76	
77	  if [[ -z "$group" ]]; then
78	    echo "Usage: glcreate-ai <group> [description] [--agent opencode|claude|codex|cursor-agent] [--lang zh|en]"
79	    echo "  Set GLCREATE_AGENT env var to change default agent (default: opencode)"
80	    echo "  Set GLCREATE_LANG  env var to change default language (default: zh)"
81	    return 1
82	  fi
83	
84	  local name=$(basename "$(pwd)")
85	  local branch=$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "main")
86	  local prompt
87	
88	  case "$lang" in
89	    en)
90	      prompt="Use glab to create a private repo under gitlab.com/${group}, repo name: ${name}, default branch: ${branch}. Set the origin remote and push.${desc:+ Description: ${desc}.} If no description is provided, summarize one sentence from the project content."
91	      ;;
92	    zh|*)
93	      prompt="用 glab 把這個 repo 建到 gitlab.com/${group} 底下，repo name: ${name}，private，default branch: ${branch}，設定 origin remote 並 push。${desc:+Description: ${desc}。}如果沒給 description 就根據項目內容總結一句。"
94	      ;;
95	  esac
96	
97	  echo "Agent: ${agent} | Lang: ${lang} | Repo: ${group}/${name} | Branch: ${branch}"
98	
99	  case "$agent" in
100	    opencode)       opencode run "$prompt" ;;
101	    claude)         claude -p "$prompt" ;;
102	    codex)          codex exec "$prompt" ;;
103	    cursor-agent)   cursor-agent -p "$prompt" ;;
104	    *)              echo "Unknown agent: ${agent}"; return 1 ;;
105	  esac
106	}
107

3	pqsum_use_color() {
4	    [[ -t 1 ]] && [[ -z "${NO_COLOR:-}" ]]
5	}
6	
7	pqsum_progress_bar() {
8	    local -i pct width filled empty
9	    pct="${1:-0}"
10	    width="${2:-12}"
11	
12	    (( pct < 0 )) && pct=0
13	    (( pct > 100 )) && pct=100
14	
15	    filled=$((pct * width / 100))
16	    empty=$((width - filled))
17	
18	    local filled_chunk empty_chunk
19	    filled_chunk="$(printf '%*s' "$filled" '' | tr ' ' '=')"
20	    empty_chunk="$(printf '%*s' "$empty" '' | tr ' ' '-')"
21	    printf '[%s%s]' "$filled_chunk" "$empty_chunk"
22	}
23	
24	pqsum_align_table() {

27	    else

29	    fi
30	}

32	# Summarize pueue status JSON into readable overall/group metrics.
33	pqsum() {
34	    local c_reset="" c_title="" c_warn="" c_err=""
35	    if pqsum_use_color; then
36	        c_reset=$'\033[0m'
37	        c_title=$'\033[1;36m'
38	        c_warn=$'\033[1;33m'
39	        c_err=$'\033[1;31m'
40	    fi
41	
42	    if ! command -v pueue &>/dev/null; then
43	        printf '%s%s%s\n' "$c_err" "pqsum: pueue not found in PATH" "$c_reset" >&2
44	        return 127
45	    fi
46	
47	    if ! command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
48	        printf '%s%s%s\n' "$c_err" "pqsum: jq not found in PATH" "$c_reset" >&2
49	        return 127
50	    fi
51	
52	    local requested_group="" idx arg
53	    for ((idx = 1; idx <= $#; idx++)); do
54	        arg="${@[$idx]}"
55	        case "$arg" in
56	            -g|--group)
57	                if (( idx < $# )); then
58	                    requested_group="${@[$((idx + 1))]}"
59	                fi
60	                ;;
61	            --group=*)
62	                requested_group="${arg#--group=}"
63	                ;;
64	        esac
65	    done
66	
67	    local pueue_json rc
68	    pueue_json="$(pueue status --json "$@")"
69	    rc=$?
70	    if (( rc != 0 )); then
71	        printf '%s%s%s\n' "$c_err" "pqsum: failed to query pueue status" "$c_reset" >&2
72	        return "$rc"
73	    fi
74	
75	    local stats_json
76	    stats_json="$(jq -c --arg requested_group "$requested_group" '
77	        def task_status:
78	          .status | keys[0];
79	
80	        def normalize_ts:
81	          sub("\\.[0-9]+"; "") as $ts
82	          | if ($ts | test("Z$")) then
83	              ($ts | sub("Z$"; "+0000"))
84	            elif ($ts | test("[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$")) then
85	              ($ts | capture("(?<prefix>.*)(?<h>[+-][0-9]{2}):(?<m>[0-9]{2})$") | "\(.prefix)\(.h)\(.m)")
86	            else
87	              $ts
88	            end;
89	
90	        def to_epoch:
91	          normalize_ts
92	          | strptime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z")
93	          | mktime;
94	
95	        def done_seconds:
96	          if (.status | has("Done")) and (.status.Done.start != null) and (.status.Done.end != null) then
97	            ((.status.Done.end | to_epoch) - (.status.Done.start | to_epoch))
98	          else
99	            null
100	          end;
101	
102	        def pct($part; $total):
103	          if $total > 0 then ($part * 100 / $total) else 0 end;
104	
105	        def fmt_pct($num):
106	          (($num * 10 | round) / 10 | tostring | if contains(".") then . else . + ".0" end) + "%";
107	
108	        def fmt_duration:
109	          if . == null then
110	            "-"
111	          else
112	            (. | floor) as $s
113	            | if $s < 60 then
114	                "\($s)s"
115	              elif $s < 3600 then
116	                "\(($s / 60 | floor))m \(($s % 60) | floor)s"
117	              else
118	                "\(($s / 3600 | floor))h \(((($s % 3600) / 60) | floor))m \(($s % 60) | floor)s"
119	              end
120	          end;
121	
122	        def status_map_to_string:
123	          if (length == 0) then
124	            "-"
125	          else
126	            (to_entries | sort_by(.key) | map("\(.key)=\(.value)") | join(", "))
127	          end;
128	
129	        (.tasks // {} | with_entries(.value |= del(.envs))) as $tasks
130	        | (.groups // {}) as $groups
131	        | ($tasks | to_entries | map(.value)) as $task_list
132	        | ($task_list | length) as $total
133	        | ($task_list | map(select(task_status == "Done")) | length) as $done
134	        | ($task_list | map(done_seconds) | map(select(. != null))) as $done_durations
135	        | ($done_durations | if length > 0 then (add / length) else null end) as $avg_done_sec
136	        | (pct($done; $total)) as $overall_pct
137	        | (
138	            if $requested_group != "" then
139	              if ($groups | has($requested_group)) or ($task_list | any((.group // "default") == $requested_group)) then
140	                [$requested_group]
141	              else
142	                []
143	              end
144	            else
145	              ((($groups | keys_unsorted) + ($task_list | map(.group // "default"))) | unique | sort)
146	            end
147	          ) as $group_names
148	        | ($task_list | sort_by(task_status) | group_by(task_status)
149	            | map({
150	                status: (.[0] | task_status),
151	                count: length,
152	                pct_num: pct(length; $total),
153	                pct: fmt_pct(pct(length; $total))
154	              })
155	          ) as $status_rows
156	        | ($group_names | map(
157	            . as $group_name
158	            | ($task_list | map(select((.group // "default") == $group_name))) as $group_tasks
159	            | ($group_tasks | length) as $group_total
160	            | ($group_tasks | map(select(task_status == "Done")) | length) as $group_done
161	            | ($group_total - $group_done) as $group_remaining
162	            | ($group_tasks | map(done_seconds) | map(select(. != null))) as $group_durations
163	            | (

172	                    | map(select(. != null))
173	                    | map(to_epoch)

175	                | if length > 0 then add else [] end
176	              ) as $group_timestamps
177	            | ($group_timestamps | if length > 0 then min else null end) as $group_first_ts
178	            | ($group_timestamps | if length > 0 then max else null end) as $group_last_ts
179	            | (
180	                if $group_first_ts != null and $group_last_ts != null then
181	                  ($group_last_ts - $group_first_ts)
182	                else

184	                end

186	            | ($group_durations | if length > 0 then (add / length) else null end) as $group_avg_sec

194	              ) as $group_parallel_for_eta
195	            | ($group_tasks | sort_by(task_status) | group_by(task_status) | map({key: (.[0] | task_status), value: length}) | from_entries) as $group_status_map
196	            | (pct($group_done; $group_total)) as $group_pct
197	            | (
198	                if $group_remaining == 0 then
199	                  (if $group_total > 0 then 0 else null end)
200	                elif $group_avg_sec == null then
201	                  null
202	                else
203	                  (($group_remaining * $group_avg_sec) / $group_parallel_for_eta)
204	                end
205	              ) as $group_eta_sec
206	            | {
207	                group: $group_name,
208	                daemon: ($groups[$group_name].status // "N/A"),
209	                parallel: ($groups[$group_name].parallel_tasks // "-"),
210	                total: $group_total,
211	                done: $group_done,
212	                pct_num: $group_pct,
213	                pct_int: ($group_pct | round),
214	                pct: fmt_pct($group_pct),
215	                total_spent: ($group_spent_sec | fmt_duration),
216	                avg_done: ($group_avg_sec | fmt_duration),
217	                eta_sec: $group_eta_sec,
218	                eta: ($group_eta_sec | fmt_duration),
219	                statuses: ($group_status_map | status_map_to_string)

223	        | (if ($overall_eta_candidates | length) > 0 then ($overall_eta_candidates | max) else null end) as $overall_eta_sec

233	              eta: ($overall_eta_sec | fmt_duration)

236	            group_rows: $group_rows
237	          }
238	    ' <<< "$pueue_json")"
239	    rc=$?

13	[[ -f "$_try_script" ]] || return 0
14	
15	eval "$(ruby "$_try_script" init)"
16	unset _try_script
17	
18	# ── try + sesh integration ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
19	# Open a try project and immediately start a sesh coding session.
20	# Usage:
21	#   try-sesh some-project       # fuzzy-match or create, then sesh connect
22	#   try-sesh https://github.com/user/repo  # clone, then sesh connect
23	#
24	# The session name follows sesh's dir_length=2 convention:
25	#   e.g. "tries/2026-04-14-some-project"
26	function try-sesh() {
27	    if ! command -v sesh &>/dev/null; then
28	        echo "try-sesh: sesh not found" >&2
29	        return 1
30	    fi
31	    # Run try, which cd's into the project directory
32	    try "$@" || return $?
33	    # Now connect sesh to the directory try landed in
34	    sesh connect "$PWD"
35	}
36	
37	alias tsesh='try-sesh'
38

28	            --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
29	            --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \
30	            --bind 'ctrl-f:change-prompt(🔎  )+reload(fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash . ~)' \
31	            --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})+change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
32	            --preview-window 'right:55%' \

38	    }
39	}

41	# Connect to a sesh session for the current directory (creates it if missing).
42	# Smart argument handling:
43	#   shere                              # default startup_command (nvim)
44	#   shere specstory run codex          # bare args → treated as command
45	#   shere -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
46	#   shere -p ~/my-proj                 # explicit path
47	#   shere -p ~/my-proj npm run dev     # explicit path + command
48	function sesh-here() {
49	    local cmd="" path=""
50	    # Parse flags first
51	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
52	        case "$1" in
53	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
54	            -p|--path)    path="$2"; shift 2 ;;
55	            -*)           echo "sesh-here: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
56	            *)            break ;;  # remaining args are the command
57	        esac
58	    done
59	    # Remaining positional args become the command
60	    [[ $# -gt 0 && -z "$cmd" ]] && cmd="$*"
61	    path="${path:-$PWD}"
62	    if [[ -n "$cmd" ]]; then
63	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$path"
64	    else
65	        sesh connect "$path"
66	    fi
67	}
68	
69	# Connect to the current git root when available, otherwise use $PWD.
70	# Same smart argument handling as sesh-here.
71	#   sroot                              # default startup_command
72	#   sroot specstory run codex          # bare args → command
73	#   sroot -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
74	function sesh-root() {
75	    local cmd="" root
76	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
77	        case "$1" in
78	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
79	            -*)           shift ;;
80	            *)            break ;;
81	        esac
82	    done
83	    [[ $# -gt 0 && -z "$cmd" ]] && cmd="$*"
84	    root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || root=$PWD
85	    if [[ -n "$cmd" ]]; then
86	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$root"
87	    else
88	        sesh connect "$root"
89	    fi
90	}
91	
92	alias shere='sesh-here'
93	alias sroot='sesh-root'
94

96	zle -N sesh-sessions
97	
98	# Key bindings (Alt+S for session switcher, avoids conflict with Ctrl+A tmux prefix)
99	bindkey -M emacs '\es' sesh-sessions
100	bindkey -M viins '\es' sesh-sessions
101	bindkey -M vicmd '\es' sesh-sessions

1	# Dotfiles Repository
2	
3	Cross-platform dotfiles management using **chezmoi** for configuration files and **ansible** for system dependencies.
4	
5	## Maintaining README.md
6	
7	**IMPORTANT**: When adding or modifying configurations, update `README.md` to reflect changes:
8	
9	- **New config files**: Add to "What You Get > Config Files" section
10	- **New ansible roles/tools**: Add to "What You Get > Tools" section
11	- **New platforms**: Add to "Supported Platforms" table
12	- **Changed setup steps**: Update "Quick Setup" section
13	
14	Keep README.md concise and user-focused. Technical details belong in CLAUDE.md or docs/.
15	
16	## Maintaining Custom Aliases & Shell Functions
17	
18	**IMPORTANT**: When adding or modifying a custom alias or shell function in any `dot_config/zsh/` file, update `docs/zsh/aliases.md`:
19	
20	- **New entry**: add a row with the command name, type (`alias` or `function`), source file (relative to repo root), and a one-line description
21	- **Modified entry**: update the existing row to reflect changes
22	- **Removed entry**: delete the row
23	
24	This keeps `docs/zsh/aliases.md` as the single quick-reference for all custom shell shortcuts.
25	
26	## Maintaining Dockerfile
27	
28	**IMPORTANT**: When adding new chezmoi prompts in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`, also update `Dockerfile`:
29	
30	1. Add corresponding `ARG CHEZMOI_*` build argument
31	2. Add `--promptBool` or `--promptString` flag to the `chezmoi init` command
32	
33	This ensures Docker testing works with all configuration options.
34	
35	## Quick Start
36	
37	```bash
38	# Install ansible (if not already installed)
39	uv tool install ansible-core
40	ansible-galaxy collection install community.general
41	
42	# Apply dotfiles
43	chezmoi apply
44	
45	# Run ansible manually (from ~/.ansible directory)
46	cd ~/.ansible && ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml
47	```
48	
49	## Architecture
50	
51	```
52	chezmoi repo/
53	├── dot_* files               → ~/.* (config files)
54	├── dot_ansible/              → ~/.ansible/ (ansible playbooks)
55	├── run_once_before_*.tmpl    → bootstrap (runs once)
56	└── run_onchange_after_*.tmpl → ansible (runs on changes)
57	```
58	
59	Installation Order:
60	
61	```
62	1. Bootstrap (run_once_before) - installs Homebrew (macOS/Linux), uv, ansible, mise
63	2. chezmoi apply - deploys config files + ansible playbooks
64	3. Ansible (run_onchange_after) - runs on fresh install + when roles change
65	4. Brew bundle (run_onchange_after) - installs GUI apps if enabled
66	```
67	
68	### Auto-run Scripts
69	
70	| Script | Behavior |
71	|--------|----------|
72	| `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl` | Installs Homebrew (macOS and Linux), uv, mise, ansible |
73	| `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` | Runs ansible with all tags |
74	| `run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl` | Runs brew bundle (if `installBrewApps` is enabled, or on macOS if `installAiDesktopApps` is enabled) |
75	
76	The onchange script includes SHA256 hashes of all role files. It runs:
77	
78	- **Fresh install**: no previous hash state → triggers run
79	- **Updates**: any role's `tasks/main.yml` or `defaults/main.yml` changes → triggers run
80	
81	To force re-run all scripts:
82	
83	```bash
84	chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=scriptState
85	chezmoi apply
86	```
87	
88	## Chezmoi Commands
89	
90	```bash
91	chezmoi diff              # Preview changes
92	chezmoi apply             # Apply changes
93	chezmoi apply --dry-run   # Test without applying
94	chezmoi edit <file>       # Edit source file
95	chezmoi cd                # Go to source directory
96	```
97	
98	## Ansible Usage
99	
100	Ansible playbooks run automatically via `chezmoi apply` when playbook files change. For manual runs, use `~/.ansible/` directory:
101	
102	```bash

104	
105	# Full setup (macOS)

107	
108	# Full setup (Linux)

110	
111	# Specific tags only

113	
114	# Skip tags requiring sudo

116	
117	# Dry run

119	```

161	## No Root Mode (Linux)
162	
163	For Linux servers where you don't have sudo/root access, enable `noRoot = true` during `chezmoi init`:
164	
165	```bash
166	chezmoi init --force  # Answer "y" to "No sudo/root access" prompt
167	```
168	
169	This skips all tasks tagged with `[sudo]` (apt packages, system-level installations). Tools with user-level fallbacks are automatically installed to `~/.local/bin` instead.
170	
171	**User-level tools** (installed automatically without sudo):
172	
173	- **GitHub binaries**: neovim, ripgrep, fd, jq, just, bat, eza, delta, yazi, zellij, btop, gitleaks, lazygit, fzf, sesh, taplo, television
174	- **mise**: Node.js, Rust runtime management
175	- **Installers**: zoxide, starship, pre-commit, thefuck, tldr
176	- **cargo tools**: pueue
177	- **uv tools**: mlflow, sqlit-tui, tmuxp, etc.
178	- **llm tools**: ollama, litellm, llmfit, models
179	- **npm tools**: Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Bitwarden CLI, etc.
180	
181	What you **won't get** without root:
182	
183	- zsh (needs `/etc/shells` for login shell)
184	- tmux, htop (require system libraries)
185	- direnv (apt only)
186	- Docker (kernel features, daemon)
187	- Ollama (system service install)
188	- System fonts (nerdfonts)
189	- Ruby and gem tools (ruby-build requires `libffi-dev` which needs sudo)
190	- build-essential, git, curl, wget, tree (assumed pre-installed)
191	
192	**Tip**: Ask your sysadmin to run: `sudo apt install git curl wget zsh tmux htop direnv build-essential tree`
193	
194	## Tmux Configuration
195	
196	The tmux config is modular under `dot_config/tmux/` (deployed to `~/.config/tmux/`), with `dot_tmux.conf` acting as a one-line shim at `~/.tmux.conf`. Structure: `tmux.conf` (entry point + theme selector), `common.conf` (plugins, general options, terminal compat), `keybindings.conf` (all binds + popup menu), `theme.catppuccin.conf` (default, top status bar), `theme.tmux2k.conf` (alternative, bottom bar).
197	
198	Theme selection priority: `$TMUX_THEME` env var → `@theme_variant` tmux option → default `catppuccin`. Switch at runtime with `prefix + M-c` (Catppuccin) or `prefix + M-t` (tmux2k). See `docs/tools/tmux/` (README, keybindings, themes, vim) for full details, including a troubleshooting note on the tmux2k bandwidth segment (`18446744073709551615K` = uint64 underflow).
199	
200	The Catppuccin status bar is **responsive**: `responsive.sh` + a `client-resized` hook dynamically adjust which modules are shown based on terminal width (>= 120 full, 80-119 medium, < 80 minimal). This makes the status bar usable on mobile terminals. See `docs/tools/tmux/themes.md` for details.
201	
202	### Key Settings for Coding Agents
203	
204	- `extended-keys always` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` -- forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, etc. through tmux to inner applications (Claude Code, Neovim, etc.)
205	- `escape-time 0` -- eliminates ESC delay for Neovim
206	- `set-clipboard on` -- OSC 52 clipboard (works over SSH)
207	- `allow-passthrough on` -- OSC passthrough for terminal images
208	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` (managed in `dot_config/ghostty/config`). See `docs/tools/ghostty.md`.
209	
210	### Tmux Keybindings
211	
212	| Binding | Action |
213	|---------|--------|
214	| `Ctrl + 1..9` | Switch to window 1–9 (no prefix, requires CSI-u terminal) |
215	| `Ctrl + 0` | Jump to git root session via sesh (no prefix, requires CSI-u) |
216	| `prefix + Space` | Native popup menu (layouts, sessions, sesh, resize, etc.) |
217	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | Navigate panes (vim-style) |
218	| `prefix + H/J/K/L` | Resize panes (5 cells) |
219	| `prefix + M-h/j/k/l` | Fine resize panes (1 cell) |
220	| `prefix + +` | Set current pane to 75% width |
221	| `prefix + \|` | Split pane left/right |
222	| `prefix + -` | Split pane top/bottom |
223	| `prefix + F` | Toggle floating pane (tmux-floax) |
224	| `prefix + P` | Floax popup menu |
225	| `prefix + u` | Open fzf URL picker (tmux-fzf-url) |
226	| `prefix + [` | Enter vim-style copy mode (v/V/y to select/yank) |
227	| `prefix + y` | Copy visible pane to clipboard |
228	| `prefix + Y` | Copy full scrollback to clipboard |
229	| `prefix + C-y` | fzf line picker from scrollback |
230	| `prefix + g` | Sesh session picker (fzf popup) |
231	| `prefix + T` | Sesh session picker (television popup) |
232	| `prefix + O` | Sesh built-in picker popup |
233	| `prefix + W` | Sesh window picker (fzf popup) |
234	| `prefix + S` | Switch to last session (sesh) |
235	| `prefix + 9` | Jump to git root session (sesh) |
236	| `prefix + N` | New session (prompts for name) |
237	| `prefix + X` | Kill session (with confirmation) |
238	| `prefix + R` | Reload tmux config |
239	| `prefix + M-c` | Switch theme to Catppuccin (top status bar) |
240	| `prefix + M-t` | Switch theme to tmux2k (bottom status bar) |
241	
242	Note: `Ctrl+Space` is NOT bound (reserved for input method switching). `Ctrl+1..9` and `Ctrl+0` require CSI-u terminal support (Ghostty/cmux, Alacritty, Kitty); legacy terminals fall back to `prefix + number`. Popup menu accelerator keys match standalone `prefix + key` bindings (see `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md` for full mapping).
243	
244	## Zellij Configuration
245	
246	Zellij config (`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl`) uses `default_mode "locked"` so all keys pass through to inner applications by default. Press `Ctrl+G` to unlock Zellij commands. This prevents key conflicts with coding agents and vim-style applications.
247	
248	On first Zellij launch (without existing config), select the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" keybinding preset for the best experience.
249	
250	## LazyVim Requirements
251	
252	- Neovim >= 0.11.2
253	- ripgrep, fd
254	- Node.js (via mise on Linux, Homebrew on macOS)
255	- tree-sitter-cli
256	- lazygit, fzf (via git on Linux, Homebrew on macOS)
257	
258	## Directory Structure
259	
260	After `chezmoi apply`:
261	
262	- Config files in `~/.*`
263	- Ansible playbooks in `~/.ansible/`
264	
265	## Development
266	
267	After modifying ansible playbooks or roles, run syntax check:
268	
269	```bash
270	ANSIBLE_CONFIG=dot_ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/base.yml
271	ANSIBLE_CONFIG=dot_ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/macos.yml
272	ANSIBLE_CONFIG=dot_ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/linux.yml
273	```
274	
275	## Ansible vs Homebrew
276	
277	**Primary tool: Ansible** - manages CLI tools and system dependencies cross-platform.
278	
279	| Tool | Role | When to Use |
280	|------|------|-------------|
281	| **Ansible** | CLI tools, system packages | Always (apt/brew formulas) |
282	| **Brewfile** | macOS GUI apps (casks), App Store | Optional (opt-in) |
283	| **Linuxbrew** | Linux packages not in apt | Always installed on Linux |
284	
285	**How they work together:**
286	
287	- Bootstrap installs Homebrew on both macOS and Linux
288	- Ansible roles use `community.general.homebrew` for macOS formulas
289	- Brewfile manages casks (GUI apps) and mas (App Store) separately
290	- On Linux, Ansible uses apt; Linuxbrew is available for newer packages
291	
292	## Brewfile (GUI Apps - Opt-in)
293	
294	GUI applications are managed via Homebrew Brewfile in XDG-compliant location `~/.config/homebrew/`.
295	
296	**Note**: Brewfile installation is **opt-in** (disabled by default). Enable general GUI apps via `chezmoi init --force` and set `installBrewApps = true`. On macOS, AI desktop apps are a separate opt-in via `installAiDesktopApps = true`.
297	
298	### File Structure
299	
300	```
301	~/.config/homebrew/
302	├── Brewfile          # Shared: taps, CLI formulas, mas
303	├── Brewfile.darwin   # macOS: casks (GUI apps), mas entries
304	└── Brewfile.linux    # Linux: linuxbrew-specific (minimal)
305	```
306	
307	### Usage
308	
309	```bash
310	# Edit Brewfiles
311	chezmoi edit ~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin
312	
313	# Apply changes manually
314	brew bundle --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile
315	brew bundle --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin
316	
317	# Or just run chezmoi apply (triggers run_onchange script)
318	chezmoi apply
319	
320	# Check what would be installed
321	brew bundle check --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin
322	```
323	
324	### Brewfile Categories (darwin)
325	
326	- **Terminals & Editors**: alacritty, iterm2, warp, cmux, cursor, visual-studio-code
327	- **AI & Coding**: claude, chatgpt, opencode-desktop, antigravity, codex-app (Apple Silicon only), and `ollama-app` when `installAiDesktopApps` + `installLlmTools`
328	- **System Utilities**: aerospace, alt-tab, raycast, jordanbaird-ice
329	- **Communication**: discord, telegram, wechat, tencent-meeting
330	- **Browsers**: arc, google-chrome, tor-browser
331	- **Productivity**: obsidian, google-drive, grammarly-desktop
332	- **Gaming**: steam, minecraft, battle-net (skipped if WORK_MACHINE env var set)
333	- **Finance**: binance, tradingview
334	- **Network**: tailscale, openvpn-connect, clash-verge-rev
335	- **Mac App Store**: LINE, Keynote, Numbers, Pages
336	
337	### Customizing Brewfile
338	
339	The Brewfiles are chezmoi templates. Conditional sections:
340	
341	- Gaming apps: skipped if `WORK_MACHINE` environment variable is set
342	- Chinese apps (baidunetdisk): only included if `useChineseMirror` is true
343	- mas apps: requires signing in to App Store.app first
344	
345	## Customization
346	
347	See [docs/ansible.md](docs/ansible.md) for detailed ansible customization guide.
348

3	Cross-platform development environment setup using **chezmoi** + **ansible**.
4	
5	- **chezmoi**: manages config files (dotfiles)
6	- **ansible**: installs system dependencies and tools

54	## Quick Setup
55	
56	```bash
57	# One-liner to initialize and apply (installs chezmoi to ~/.local/bin)
58	export GITHUB_USERNAME=daviddwlee84
59	sh -c "$(curl -fsLS get.chezmoi.io)" -- -b "$HOME/.local/bin" init --apply git@github.com:$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git
60	```
61	
62	This automatically:
63	
64	1. Bootstraps Homebrew (macOS/Linux), uv, mise, ansible
65	2. Deploys all config files
66	3. Runs ansible playbooks (git, ripgrep, fd, neovim, etc.)
67	4. Runs brew bundle (if `installBrewApps` is enabled, or on macOS if `installAiDesktopApps` is enabled)

69	### After install
70	
71	- `~/.local/bin` is auto-appended to `~/.bashrc` so `chezmoi`, `uv`, and `mise` stay reachable from bash.
72	- On sudo-enabled machines, the ansible `zsh` role switches your login shell to zsh automatically. Log out / back in to pick it up, or run `exec zsh` now.
73	- On `noRoot=true` installs, login shell isn't changed — run `exec zsh` per session, or ask your sysadmin: `sudo chsh -s "$(command -v zsh)" $USER`.
74	- Open a new shell (or `source ~/.bashrc`) after install so PATH changes take effect.
75	
76	### Optional Components
77

90	| `noRoot` | false | Skip sudo-requiring tasks (for servers without root access) |

1	# 10_fzf.zsh - fzf configuration
2	
3	# Add git-installed fzf to PATH if present
4	[[ -d "$HOME/.fzf/bin" ]] && export PATH="$HOME/.fzf/bin:$PATH"
5	
6	# Check if fzf is installed
7	command -v fzf &>/dev/null || return 0
8	
9	# Load fzf shell integration
10	# fzf 0.48.0+ supports --zsh flag, older versions need separate script files
11	if fzf --zsh &>/dev/null; then
12	    source <(fzf --zsh)
13	elif [[ -f ~/.fzf.zsh ]]; then
14	    # Git-installed fzf (if install script was run with shell integration)
15	    source ~/.fzf.zsh
16	elif [[ -f /usr/share/doc/fzf/examples/key-bindings.zsh ]]; then
17	    # Debian/Ubuntu apt-installed fzf (fallback for old versions)
18	    source /usr/share/doc/fzf/examples/key-bindings.zsh
19	    [[ -f /usr/share/doc/fzf/examples/completion.zsh ]] && source /usr/share/doc/fzf/examples/completion.zsh
20	fi
21	
22	# Default options
23	export FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS="--height 40% --layout=reverse --border"
24	
25	# Use fd for fzf if available (faster than find)
26	if command -v fd &>/dev/null; then
27	    export FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND="fd --hidden --strip-cwd-prefix --exclude .git"
28	    export FZF_CTRL_T_COMMAND="$FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND"
29	    export FZF_ALT_C_COMMAND="fd --type=d --hidden --strip-cwd-prefix --exclude .git"
30	fi
31	
32	# Use bat for file preview (Ctrl+T) if available
33	if command -v bat &>/dev/null; then
34	    export FZF_CTRL_T_OPTS="--preview 'bat -n --color=always --line-range :500 {}'"
35	fi
36	
37	# Use eza for directory preview (Alt+C) if available
38	if command -v eza &>/dev/null; then
39	    export FZF_ALT_C_OPTS="--preview 'eza --tree --color=always {} | head -200'"
40	fi
41	
42	# Advanced: Tab completion preview behavior
43	_fzf_comprun() {
44	    local command=$1
45	    shift
46	
47	    case "$command" in
48	        cd)
49	            if command -v eza &>/dev/null; then
50	                fzf --preview 'eza --tree --color=always {} | head -200' "$@"
51	            else
52	                fzf --preview 'tree -C {} | head -200' "$@"
53	            fi
54	            ;;
55	        export|unset)
56	            fzf --preview "eval 'echo \$'{}" "$@"
57	            ;;
58	        ssh)
59	            fzf --preview 'dig {}' "$@"
60	            ;;
61	        *)
62	            if command -v bat &>/dev/null; then
63	                fzf --preview 'bat -n --color=always --line-range :500 {}' "$@"
64	            else
65	                fzf --preview 'head -500 {}' "$@"
66	            fi
67	            ;;
68	    esac
69	}

1	# 22_sesh.zsh - sesh tmux session manager
2	# https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh
3	
4	# Check if sesh is installed
5	command -v sesh &>/dev/null || return 0
6	
7	# Auto-generate shell completion into ~/.zfunc/ (regenerates on version change)
8	if [[ -d ~/.zfunc ]]; then
9	    local _sesh_ver="$(sesh --version 2>/dev/null)"
10	    if [[ ! -f ~/.zfunc/_sesh ]] || ! grep -q "${_sesh_ver}" ~/.zfunc/_sesh 2>/dev/null; then
11	        sesh completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_sesh 2>/dev/null
12	    fi
13	fi
14	
15	# Sesh session switcher with fzf (full-featured picker)
16	# Supports icons, preview, filtering by source, and session killing
17	function sesh-sessions() {
18	    {
19	        exec </dev/tty
20	        exec <&1
21	        local session
22	        session=$(sesh list --icons | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% \
23	            --no-sort --ansi --border-label ' sesh ' --prompt '⚡  ' \
24	            --header '  ^a all ^t tmux ^g configs ^x zoxide ^d tmux kill ^f find' \
25	            --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
26	            --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
27	            --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
28	            --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
29	            --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \
30	            --bind 'ctrl-f:change-prompt(🔎  )+reload(fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash . ~)' \
31	            --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})+change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
32	            --preview-window 'right:55%' \
33	            --preview 'sesh preview {}' \
34	        )
35	        zle reset-prompt > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
36	        [[ -z "$session" ]] && return
37	        sesh connect "$session"
38	    }
39	}
40	
41	# Connect to a sesh session for the current directory (creates it if missing).
42	# Smart argument handling:
43	#   shere                              # default startup_command (nvim)
44	#   shere specstory run codex          # bare args → treated as command
45	#   shere -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
46	#   shere -p ~/my-proj                 # explicit path
47	#   shere -p ~/my-proj npm run dev     # explicit path + command
48	function sesh-here() {
49	    local cmd="" path=""
50	    # Parse flags first
51	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
52	        case "$1" in
53	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
54	            -p|--path)    path="$2"; shift 2 ;;
55	            -*)           echo "sesh-here: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
56	            *)            break ;;  # remaining args are the command
57	        esac
58	    done
59	    # Remaining positional args become the command
60	    [[ $# -gt 0 && -z "$cmd" ]] && cmd="$*"
61	    path="${path:-$PWD}"
62	    if [[ -n "$cmd" ]]; then
63	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$path"
64	    else
65	        sesh connect "$path"
66	    fi
67	}
68	
69	# Connect to the current git root when available, otherwise use $PWD.
70	# Same smart argument handling as sesh-here.
71	#   sroot                              # default startup_command
72	#   sroot specstory run codex          # bare args → command
73	#   sroot -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
74	function sesh-root() {
75	    local cmd="" root
76	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
77	        case "$1" in
78	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
79	            -*)           shift ;;
80	            *)            break ;;
81	        esac
82	    done
83	    [[ $# -gt 0 && -z "$cmd" ]] && cmd="$*"
84	    root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || root=$PWD
85	    if [[ -n "$cmd" ]]; then
86	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$root"
87	    else
88	        sesh connect "$root"
89	    fi
90	}
91	
92	alias shere='sesh-here'
93	alias sroot='sesh-root'
94	
95	# Register as zsh widget
96	zle -N sesh-sessions
97	
98	# Key bindings (Alt+S for session switcher, avoids conflict with Ctrl+A tmux prefix)
99	bindkey -M emacs '\es' sesh-sessions
100	bindkey -M viins '\es' sesh-sessions
101	bindkey -M vicmd '\es' sesh-sessions
102

30	# but installing ca-certificates from default repos fails under GFW

41	            "URIs: ${MIRROR_URL}" \

43	            "Components: main restricted universe multiverse" \
44	            "Signed-By: /usr/share/keyrings/ubuntu-archive-keyring.gpg" \
45	            "" \
46	            "Types: deb" \

27	# command -v eza &>/dev/null && alias ls="eza"
28	# command -v bat &>/dev/null && alias cat="bat"
29	
30	# Git shortcuts
31	gcam() {
32	  [[ -z "$1" ]] && { echo "Usage: gcam <message>"; return 1; }
33	  git add -A && git commit -m "$1"
34	}
35	
36	# Amend last commit (keep message by default; pass -m "new msg" to change it)
37	alias gca='git commit --amend --no-edit'
38	gcam-amend() {
39	  [[ -z "$1" ]] && { echo "Usage: gcam-amend <new message>"; return 1; }
40	  git commit --amend -m "$1"
41	}
42	
43	# Undo last commit → back to staged, print the undone commit message
44	gundo() {
45	  local msg
46	  msg="$(git log -1 --pretty=%B)" || return 1
47	  git reset --soft HEAD~1 && echo "Undone commit:\n  $msg"
48	}
49	
50	# Zsh startup profiling
51	alias zsh-profile='ZSH_PROF=1 zsh -i -c exit'
52	
53	# Load NVM for current session (when needed for version switching)
54	alias load-nvm='export LOAD_NVM=1 && source "${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}/nvm.sh" && source "${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}/bash_completion" && echo "nvm loaded: $(nvm current)"'
55	
56	# Regenerate cached bw completion (run after updating bw CLI)
57	alias bw-update-completion='mkdir -p "${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/zsh" && bw completion --shell zsh > "${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/zsh/bw_completion.zsh" 2>/dev/null && echo "bw completion cache updated"'
58	
59	# Install Ghostty terminfo on a remote host (unprivileged, into ~/.terminfo).
60	# Fixes character-rendering issues when SSH'ing into a fresh host from Ghostty/cmux/tmux.
61	# Usage: ghostty-ssh-terminfo <ssh-host>
62	ghostty-ssh-terminfo() {
63	  emulate -L zsh
64	  setopt pipefail
65	
66	  local host="$1"
67	
68	  if [[ -z "$host" ]]; then
69	    echo "Usage: ghostty-ssh-terminfo <ssh-host>" >&2
70	    return 1
71	  fi
72	
73	  if ! command -v infocmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then
74	    echo "ghostty-ssh-terminfo: local 'infocmp' not found" >&2
75	    return 1
76	  fi
77	
78	  if ! infocmp -x xterm-ghostty >/dev/null 2>&1; then
79	    echo "ghostty-ssh-terminfo: local terminfo 'xterm-ghostty' not found" >&2
80	    return 1
81	  fi
82	
83	  if ! infocmp -x xterm-ghostty \
84	      | ssh "$host" '
85	          set -e
86	          if ! command -v tic >/dev/null 2>&1; then
87	            echo "remote: tic not found" >&2
88	            exit 127
89	          fi
90	          mkdir -p "$HOME/.terminfo"
91	          TERMINFO="$HOME/.terminfo" tic -x -
92	        ' 2> >(grep -Fv "older tic versions may treat the description field as an alias" >&2); then
93	    echo "ghostty-ssh-terminfo: failed to install on $host" >&2
94	    return 1
95	  fi
96	
97	  echo "Installed xterm-ghostty terminfo on $host (in ~/.terminfo)"
98	}
99

```text
1	# Zsh Completions Best Practices
2	
3	How zsh tab completions are organized in this dotfiles project.
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	```
8	compinit runs once (inside oh-my-zsh.sh)
9	        │
10	        ├── ~/.zfunc/                          ← user-generated completions (NOT tracked by chezmoi)
11	        ├── ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/       ← community completions (184 files, cloned by ansible)
12	        │     └── zsh-completions/src/
13	        ├── ~/.docker/completions/             ← Docker-shipped completions
14	        ├── $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/        ← Homebrew-managed completions (via `brew completions link`)
15	        │     └── site-functions/
16	        └── $ZSH/completions/                  ← oh-my-zsh built-in completions
17	```
18	
19	All `fpath` additions are in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` **before** `source "$ZSH/oh-my-zsh.sh"`, so `compinit` runs exactly once and picks up everything.
20	
21	## Completion Categories
22	
23	Tools fall into four categories:
24	
25	### A. Self-generating (`tool completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_tool`)
26	
27	Most modern CLI tools can output their own completion script. Run once after install, re-run after version upgrades.
28	
29	| Tool | Command |
30	|------|---------|
31	| `uv` | `uv generate-shell-completion zsh` |
32	| `mise` | `mise completion zsh` |
33	| `chezmoi` | `chezmoi completion zsh` |
34	| `just` | `just --completions zsh` |
35	| `bat` | `bat --completion zsh` |
36	| `delta` | `delta --generate-completion zsh` |
37	| `starship` | `starship completions zsh` |
38	| `rg` | `rg --generate complete-zsh` |
39	| `fd` | `fd --gen-completions zsh` |
40	| `zellij` | `zellij setup --generate-completion zsh` |
41	| `sesh` | `sesh completion zsh` |
42	| `pueue` | `pueue completions zsh` |
43	| `docker` | `docker completion zsh` |
44	| `gh` | `gh completion -s zsh` |
45	| `opencode` | `opencode completion zsh` |
46	| `bw` | `bw completion --shell zsh` |
47	
48	**Usage pattern:**
49	
50	```bash
51	# Generate once (or after upgrade)
52	mkdir -p ~/.zfunc
53	uv generate-shell-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_uv
54	mise completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_mise
55	```
56	
57	### B. Pre-bundled (no action needed)
58	
59	Completions ship with the package or via the `zsh-completions` community plugin.
60	
61	| Tool | Source |
62	|------|--------|
63	| `eza` | Homebrew formula installs `_eza` into site-functions |
64	| `git` | oh-my-zsh `git` plugin |
65	| `yazi` | Ships `_yazi` in release assets (also in zsh-completions) |
66	| `lazygit` | No completion support; not needed (TUI app) |
67	| `btop` | No completion support; not needed (TUI app) |
68	| Many others | `zsh-completions` plugin covers 184 tools |
69	
70	### C. Eval/source at startup (shell integration)
71	
72	These tools inject completions as part of broader shell integration. Already handled in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`.
73	
74	| Tool | Where | How |
75	|------|-------|-----|
76	| `fzf` | `tools/10_fzf.zsh` | `source <(fzf --zsh)` |
77	| `zoxide` | `tools/20_zoxide.zsh` | `eval "$(zoxide init zsh)"` |
78	| `thefuck` | `tools/25_thefuck.zsh` | `eval $(thefuck --alias)` |
79	| `direnv` | `tools/30_direnv.zsh` | `eval "$(direnv hook zsh)"` |
80	| `marimo` | `tools/29_marimo.zsh` | `eval "$(_MARIMO_COMPLETE=zsh_source marimo)"` |
81	
82	### D. No completion support
83	
84	`claude`, `gemini`, `btop`, `lazygit` -- no generation command available.
85	
86	### E. Python tools via `shtab` / `tyro`
87	
88	Python CLI frameworks can generate completions:
89	
90	- **[tyro](https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/tab_completion/)**: `python my_cli.py --tyro-write-completion zsh ~/.zfunc/_my_cli`
91	- **[shtab](https://github.com/iterative/shtab)**: `shtab --shell=zsh my_module.parser > ~/.zfunc/_my_tool`
92	- **argcomplete**: `register-python-argcomplete tool_name` (uses eval, category C)
93	- **click** (used by mlflow, litellm, etc.): `_TOOL_COMPLETE=zsh_source tool > ~/.zfunc/_tool`
94	
95	## Why `~/.zfunc/` is NOT Tracked by Chezmoi
96	
97	**Decision: `~/.zfunc/` is not version-controlled.** Rationale:
98	
99	1. **Completions are tool-version-dependent.** A completion script generated by `uv 0.6` may not match `uv 0.7`. Tracking stale files causes subtle breakage.
100	2. **Not all users install the same tools.** A `_pueue` completion file is useless (and throws warnings) if pueue isn't installed.
101	3. **Regeneration is trivial.** One command per tool.
102	4. **Brew-installed tools auto-manage their completions** via site-functions. Duplicating them in `~/.zfunc/` creates conflicts.
103	
104	### What we DO track
105	
106	- `fpath+=~/.zfunc` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` (ensures the directory is in the search path)
107	- `zsh-completions` plugin cloned by ansible (community completions)
108	- `~/.docker/completions` fpath entry
109	- Tool-specific `eval`/`source` integrations in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`
110	
111	## Generating Completions After Fresh Install
112	
113	After `chezmoi apply` on a new machine, most completions already work via `zsh-completions` plugin and Homebrew site-functions. For tools you want **richer/newer completions**, generate them into `~/.zfunc/`:
114	
115	```bash
116	mkdir -p ~/.zfunc
117	
118	# Core tools (always installed)
119	chezmoi completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_chezmoi
120	mise completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_mise
121	uv generate-shell-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_uv
122	just --completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_just
123	starship completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_starship
124	
125	# Dev tools (if installed)
126	command -v gh    && gh completion -s zsh > ~/.zfunc/_gh
127	command -v docker && docker completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_docker
128	command -v rg    && rg --generate complete-zsh > ~/.zfunc/_rg
129	command -v fd    && fd --gen-completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_fd
130	command -v bat   && bat --completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_bat
131	command -v delta && delta --generate-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_delta
132	command -v zellij && zellij setup --generate-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_zellij
133	command -v sesh  && sesh completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_sesh
134	command -v pueue && pueue completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_pueue
135	
136	# Coding agents (if installed)
137	command -v opencode && opencode completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_opencode
138	command -v bw    && bw completion --shell zsh > ~/.zfunc/_bw
139	
140	# Force rebuild completion cache
141	rm -f ~/.zcompdump && compinit
142	```
143	
144	> **Tip:** You can save this as a script in `~/.local/bin/` or add it to `~/.zshrc.adhoc` as a function.
145	
146	## Priority / Override Order
147	
148	When the same `_tool` file exists in multiple fpath directories, the **first match wins**:
149	
150	```
151	1. ~/.zfunc/                                    (highest - your overrides)
152	2. ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/
153	3. ~/.docker/completions/
154	4. $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/   (Homebrew-managed)
155	5. /usr/share/zsh/*/functions/                  (system, lowest)
156	```
157	
158	Current `dot_zshrc.tmpl` order:
159	
160	```zsh
161	fpath+=~/.zfunc                     # appended (lowest of custom)
162	fpath=(zsh-completions/src $fpath)  # prepended (higher than ~/.zfunc)
163	fpath=(~/.docker/completions $fpath) # prepended (highest of custom)
164	```
165	
166	If you want `~/.zfunc/` to override community completions, change to prepend:
167	
168	```zsh
169	fpath=(~/.zfunc $fpath)  # prepend instead of append
170	```
171	
172	## FAQ
173	
174	**Q: Should I generate completions for tools that `zsh-completions` already covers?**
175	A: Only if you want the latest version. The community plugin may lag behind. For fast-moving tools (uv, mise), generating your own is worthwhile.
176	
177	**Q: A completion file throws errors after I uninstall a tool. What do I do?**
178	A: Remove the file: `rm ~/.zfunc/_toolname`. Stale `_tool` files in fpath are harmless (silently ignored) unless they have syntax errors.
179	
180	**Q: How do I debug completion issues?**
181	A: Run `echo $fpath | tr ' ' '\n'` to see all fpath entries. Use `which _toolname` to see which completion file is being used. Force rebuild with `rm -f ~/.zcompdump && compinit`.
182
```

## 2. FZF CONFIGURATION

**File:** `/home/keithkslee/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/zsh/tools/10_fzf.zsh`

### **Shell Integration**

### **Environment Variables**
```bash
FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS="--height 40% --layout=reverse --border"

# Use fd instead of find (faster)
FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND="fd --hidden --strip-cwd-prefix --exclude .git"
FZF_CTRL_T_COMMAND="$FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND"                                    # File picker
FZF_ALT_C_COMMAND="fd --type=d --hidden --strip-cwd-prefix --exclude .git"  # Dir picker

# File preview (Ctrl+T) using bat
FZF_CTRL_T_OPTS="--preview 'bat -n --color=always --line-range :500 {}'"

# Directory preview (Alt+C) using eza
FZF_ALT_C_OPTS="--preview 'eza --tree --color=always {} | head -200'"
```

### **Built-in Keybindings** (from fzf shell integration)
- `Ctrl+T` — Fuzzy file picker (insert selected file into command line)
- `Ctrl+R` — Fuzzy command history
- `Alt+C` — Fuzzy directory picker and cd

### **Custom Completion Preview** (`_fzf_comprun` function)
Command-specific previews for tab completion:
- `cd` — eza tree or fallback to tree
- `export`/`unset` — Show variable value
- `ssh` — DNS lookup via dig
- **Default** — bat syntax highlighting (500 lines)

### **No Custom Keybindings Defined**
The repo uses fzf's default keybindings; custom bindings are added elsewhere for sesh/television integration (see below).

# Project Maintenance Cheatsheet

Quick reference for all CLI commands used to maintain this dotfiles repo.

> Most commands have a `just` shortcut. Run `just` (no args) to list every available recipe.

---

## Table of Contents

- [just](#just)
- [chezmoi](#chezmoi)
- [Ansible](#ansible)
- [Brew Bundle](#brew-bundle)
- [Docker](#docker)
- [Pre-commit & Gitleaks](#pre-commit--gitleaks)

---

## just

\```bash
just          # List all available recipes
just info     # Show system info and installed tool versions
just status   # git status
just diff     # git diff
just check    # Full lint + dry-run (run before commits)
\```

---

## chezmoi

| Command | `just` shortcut | Description |
|---------|-----------------|-------------|
| `chezmoi diff` | `just chezmoi-diff` | Preview what would change |
| `chezmoi apply` | `just chezmoi-apply` | Deploy dotfiles and trigger run scripts |
| `chezmoi apply --dry-run` | `just chezmoi-dry-run` | Test apply without making changes |
| `chezmoi status` | `just chezmoi-status` | Show modified/added/removed files |
| `chezmoi edit <file>` | — | Edit a source file (e.g. `chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc`) |
| `chezmoi cd` | — | Jump to the chezmoi source directory |
| `chezmoi init` | `just chezmoi-reinit` | Re-run interactive init prompts |
| `chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=scriptState` | `just chezmoi-clear-scripts` | Reset run_once script state |
| *(clear + apply)* | `just chezmoi-rerun-scripts` | Clear script state then re-apply |

---

## Ansible

Playbooks live in `~/.ansible/` after `chezmoi apply` (source: `dot_ansible/`).

\```bash
cd ~/.ansible

# Full platform setup
ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml                    # macOS
ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml --ask-become-pass  # Linux (sudo)
ansible-playbook playbooks/base.yml                     # Core tools only

# Selective runs
ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --tags "neovim,lazyvim_deps"
ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml --skip-tags "sudo"

# Dry run
ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --check

# Syntax check (from repo root)
ANSIBLE_CONFIG=dot_ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/macos.yml
ANSIBLE_CONFIG=dot_ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/linux.yml
\```

**`just` shortcuts:**

\```bash
just ansible-syntax-check         # Check all playbooks
just ansible-base                 # Run base playbook
just ansible-macos                # Run macOS playbook
just ansible-linux                # Run Linux playbook
just ansible-tags "neovim,zsh"    # Run specific tags only
just ansible-check                # Dry run (--check)
just ansible-security             # security_tools tag only
\```

### Available Ansible Tags

| Tag | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| `base` | git, curl, ripgrep, fd, build tools |
| `zsh` | zsh, oh-my-zsh, plugins |
| `starship` | Starship cross-shell prompt |
| `neovim` | Neovim (>= 0.11.2) |
| `lazyvim_deps` | fzf, lazygit, tree-sitter-cli, Node.js |
| `devtools` | bat, eza, delta, zoxide, tmux, sesh, zellij, btop, television, yazi, … |
| `docker` | Docker / OrbStack |
| `nerdfonts` | Hack Nerd Font |
| `security_tools` | pre-commit, gitleaks |
| `homebrew` | macOS Homebrew update *(macOS only)* |
| `coding_agents` | Claude Code, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI, etc. *(opt-in)* |
| `bitwarden` | Bitwarden CLI + Desktop *(opt-in)* |
| `python_uv_tools` | uv-managed CLI tools *(opt-in)* |
| `llm_tools` | Ollama, LiteLLM, llmfit *(opt-in)* |
| `rust_cargo_tools` | pueue, etc. via cargo |
| `ruby_gem_tools` | try-cli, tmuxinator via gem |
| `input_method` | McBopomofo + RIME *(desktop + opt-in)* |
| `networking_tools` | nmap, doggo, httpie, bandwhich, rustscan, … *(opt-in)* |

---

## Brew Bundle

GUI apps are opt-in (`installBrewApps = true` during `chezmoi init`).

\```bash
# Check what's missing
brew bundle check --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile
brew bundle check --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin

# Install
brew bundle --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile
brew bundle --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin   # macOS casks + mas
brew bundle --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.linux    # Linuxbrew packages

# Edit (opens source file via chezmoi)
chezmoi edit ~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin
\```

> `chezmoi apply` triggers Brew Bundle automatically when Brewfile content changes.

---

## Docker

Used for testing the full setup on a bare Ubuntu image.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `just docker-build` | Build default image (ubuntu_server) |
| `just docker-build-all` | Build server + desktop + china profiles |
| `just docker-run` | Interactive shell in devbox container |
| `just docker-up` | Start devbox container in background |
| `just docker-down` | Stop all containers |
| `just docker-test` | Run full test suite in container |
| `just docker-desktop` | Build + enter desktop profile |
| `just docker-china` | Build + enter china profile (Chinese mirrors) |
| `just docker-clean` | Remove all dotfiles containers and images |

---

## Pre-commit & Gitleaks

\```bash
# Setup
just pre-commit-install-tool   # Install pre-commit binary
just pre-commit-setup          # Install git hooks in repo

# Run
just pre-commit-run            # Run on staged files
just pre-commit-run-all        # Run on all files
just pre-commit-update         # Update hook versions
just pre-commit-uninstall      # Remove git hooks

# Secret scanning
just gitleaks-scan             # Scan working tree for secrets
just gitleaks-scan-history     # Scan full git history
just check-specstory           # Check .specstory files for secrets
just redact-specstory          # Auto-redact secrets in .specstory files
\```

# fzf Quick Reference

[fzf](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf) — command-line fuzzy finder.

Config source: `dot_config/zsh/tools/10_fzf.zsh`

---

## Shell Keybindings

| Key | Action | Preview |
|-----|--------|---------|
| `Ctrl+T` | Insert fuzzy-matched file path at cursor | `bat` syntax highlight (500 lines) |
| `Ctrl+R` | Fuzzy search command history | — |
| `Alt+C` | Fuzzy-match directory and `cd` into it | `eza --tree` (200 lines) |

---

## Environment Variables

\```bash
# Base options applied to all fzf invocations
FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS="--height 40% --layout=reverse --border"

# Use fd instead of find (respects .gitignore, faster)
FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND="fd --hidden --strip-cwd-prefix --exclude .git"

# Ctrl+T: file picker
FZF_CTRL_T_COMMAND="fd --hidden --strip-cwd-prefix --exclude .git"
FZF_CTRL_T_OPTS="--preview 'bat -n --color=always --line-range :500 {}'"

# Alt+C: directory picker
FZF_ALT_C_COMMAND="fd --type=d --hidden --strip-cwd-prefix --exclude .git"
FZF_ALT_C_OPTS="--preview 'eza --tree --color=always {} | head -200'"
\```

---

## Tab Completion Preview (`_fzf_comprun`)

When using fzf-powered tab completion, preview varies by command:

| Command | Preview |
|---------|---------|
| `cd` | `eza --tree --color=always` (fallback: `tree -C`) |
| `export`, `unset` | `echo ${<var>}` — shows current variable value |
| `ssh` | `dig <host>` — DNS lookup |
| *(default)* | `bat -n --color=always --line-range :500` |

---

## fzf-tmux Integration

The `sesh-sessions` widget (bound to `Alt+S`) uses `fzf-tmux -p 80%,70%` to open a
floating popup inside tmux. See `docs/tools/sesh.md` for session picker keybindings.

---

## Tips

- **Fuzzy syntax**: space-separated tokens are AND'd; `!` negates; `^` anchors start; `$` anchors end
  - Example: `^foo bar !baz$` — starts with "foo", contains "bar", does not end with "baz"
- **Multi-select**: pass `--multi` (or `-m`) to enable `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` for multi-selection
- **Preview toggle**: `Ctrl+/` toggles the preview pane (built-in default)

```

# television (tv) Quick Reference

[television](https://github.com/alexpasmantier/television) — blazing-fast TUI fuzzy finder with pluggable "channels".

Config source: `dot_config/television/cable/sesh.toml`

---

## Basic Usage

\```bash
tv                   # Open interactive picker (default channel)
tv <channel>         # Open a specific channel, e.g. tv sesh
tv --help            # List all flags
\```

From tmux: `prefix + T` opens the sesh channel as a popup (see [Tmux Integration](#tmux-integration)).

---

## Custom Channels

### `sesh` channel

Overrides the built-in sesh channel with richer source cycling and session management.

**Source cycling keybindings** (shown in picker header):

| Key | Source | Description |
|-----|--------|-------------|
| `Ctrl+A` | All sessions | `sesh list --icons` |
| `Ctrl+T` | Tmux sessions | `sesh list -t --icons` |
| `Ctrl+G` | Configured sessions | `sesh list -c --icons` |
| `Ctrl+X` | Zoxide directories | `sesh list -z --icons` |
| `Ctrl+F` | File search | `fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash ~` |

**Action keybindings:**

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `Enter` | Connect to selected session |
| `Ctrl+D` | Kill selected tmux session + refresh list |

**Preview:** `sesh preview '{selection}'` — right panel, 55% width.

---

## Tmux Integration

| Binding | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `prefix + T` | Open sesh channel as a television popup |
| `prefix + g` | Open sesh session picker via fzf (alternative) |

> For the full tmux session management keybinding reference, see `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.

---

## Tips

- `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` — navigate results
- `Ctrl+P` / `Ctrl+N` — move up/down (vim users)
- Channels are defined as `.toml` files in `~/.config/television/cable/`
- Custom channels in this repo live at `dot_config/television/cable/` (deployed via chezmoi)
